content: Acetaminophen and codeine is a combination medication prescribed to alleviate mild to moderate pain. It may also be used for other purposes as determined by your doctor. If you have questions about its use, consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist. This medication is available in tablet, capsule, and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken every six hours as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take acetaminophen and codeine exactly as directed. Codeine has the potential to be habit-forming, so do not take a larger dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed by your doctor. Before taking acetaminophen and codeine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acetaminophen, codeine, sulfites, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially acetaminophen (e.g., Tylenol), antidepressants, medications for cough, cold, or allergies, other pain relievers, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had liver or kidney disease, a history of alcoholism, lung or thyroid disease, prostate enlargement, or urinary retention. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental surgery, inform your surgeon or dentist that you are taking acetaminophen and codeine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. If you forget to take a dose, this medication is usually taken as needed. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take it regularly, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Acetaminophen and codeine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: dizziness, lightheadedness, drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, rash, or difficulty urinating. If you experience severe side effects such as difficulty breathing or mood changes, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Excessive acetaminophen use can cause liver damage; do not exceed 4000 mg of acetaminophen per day. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
